**(1) First message**

```text
gauntlet: question
One premise is contradicted. Ticket acme/widgets#77 requires an owner column in the export, but the export has no owner column today: src/export/csv.ts:40 defines the columns as `["title", "status"]` only. The design starts from that fact, and you can override it in your reply.

Some claims are supported. src/export/csv.ts exists and holds the column list at line 40. The overrides `## Issue tracker` section names this repo as acme/widgets, and the ticket has no repo groups, so I'm assuming all three rows belong here.

Some claims are unverified:
- The draft says the reports page renders a table with no export action. The page source is not in the files I have, so I could not read it.
- The draft says csv.ts reuses the table's column definitions. I saw only line 40, so I could not trace other consumers of `tableColumns`.
- I could not check whether report records carry an owner field at all.
- The 10k-row-under-60s row depends on a 10k-row report fixture to verify against. I looked for one and found nothing in the supplied files.

I'll carry each of these as an Open Question or a stated assumption.

The framing holds: I checked the export path's column source at src/export/csv.ts:40 and the draft's claim that the export reuses the table columns. I also checked the ask's implicit dependencies (an owner field on report data, a 10k-row fixture), and neither is in the supplied files. The draft carries no `Framing:` line, so this check comes from my own recon. Its pattern note offers no alternative to the ask, because an export module already exists and the missing piece is the page action, which is what the ticket asks for.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
A) beside the report title
B) in the table's header toolbar
C) in the page's overflow menu
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - it is the page-level action spot and needs no new toolbar or menu.
```

**(2) Approaches message**

```text
gauntlet: question
First, the implicit dependencies that are missing or could not be checked:
- Owner data: I looked for an owner field on report records in the supplied files and found none. Its existence is unverified.
- 10k-row fixture: I looked for a 10k-row report fixture to verify the timing row and found none in the supplied files. The spec will have to add a generated fixture.
- Other consumers of `tableColumns`: tracing them requires the reports page source, which was not supplied. The blast radius of changing that list is unverified.

You chose to repair the ticket for the owner row, and that repair was cancelled at the shape-ticket gate, so row 2 still reads as written. Until you answer the question at the end, I'm treating it as in-scope (the default), and both approaches below satisfy it.

Recommendation: approach 1. The export gets its own column list built from the table's, and the table stays as it is today.

1) Export extends the table columns. In csv.ts, an export column list is built as the table's columns plus `owner`. The button beside the report title calls the existing export with that list. The table keeps showing title and status only, so the ticket's change stays limited to the export, which is all the ticket asks for. The cost is that the export is no longer an exact mirror of the table.
Removes: none
Adds: an `exportColumns` constant in src/export/csv.ts derived from `tableColumns`; an owner value accessor; an Export CSV button beside the report title; a CSV test asserting the owner column; a 10k-row generated-fixture test asserting completion under 60s
Pattern: follows the reuse at src/export/csv.ts:40 by deriving from `tableColumns`, not copying it, but it breaks the export-equals-table contract the draft notes.

2) Add owner to the shared list. `owner` goes into `tableColumns` at src/export/csv.ts:40, so the table and the export both gain the column. This keeps a single column contract. The blast radius is every consumer of `tableColumns`, which I could not trace: at minimum the table visibly gains an owner column the ticket never asked for.
Removes: none
Adds: an `"owner"` entry in `tableColumns`; an owner accessor and owner cell rendering in the table; an Export CSV button beside the report title; a table render test for the owner column; a CSV test asserting the owner column; a 10k-row generated-fixture test asserting completion under 60s
Pattern: keeps the single shared column definition at src/export/csv.ts:40, with blast radius across every unverified consumer of `tableColumns`.

Two other candidates I considered are not viable:
- Reuse-only (wiring the button to the existing export with `tableColumns` unchanged) is not viable while row 2 is in-scope. The only column source, src/export/csv.ts:40, lacks owner.
- Dropping the ask's assumption of a direct in-page export in favour of a streamed or background export is also not viable as a distinct approach. Nothing supplied shows the current export path missing the 60s bound, and the fixture that would show it does not exist yet.

What would flip my recommendation to approach 2: you want owner visible on the reports table as well, or tracing shows other `tableColumns` consumers that must stay in lockstep with the export.

The repair was cancelled, so the owner-row question comes back with the row unchanged:
For the owner-column row ("The export includes the owner column."), src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column. How should the spec carry it?
A) in-scope - add owner to the export (approach 1 or 2 above)
B) deviates: omit owner
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 row "The export includes the owner column.", because src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column
Recommendation: A - adding owner is a bounded change on the export path, so the row can ship in this gauntlet without waiting on a ticket repair.
```
